exponential-and-ordering.title: Exponential Limits and the Standard Growth Hierarchy
exponential-and-ordering.bodyMarkdown:
### Exponential comparisons

9. `2ⁿ / (10n²) → ∞`, so `2ⁿ = Ω(10n²)`. A correct two-step L’Hôpital calculation includes the factors `ln 2` and the derivative `20n`.

10. `2ⁿ / 2²ⁿ = 2⁻ⁿ → 0`, so `2ⁿ = O(2²ⁿ)`.

11. `2ⁿ / 3ⁿ = (2/3)ⁿ → 0`, so `2ⁿ = O(3ⁿ)`.

### Order the functions

From slowest to fastest as `n → ∞`:

$$
\log n < \sqrt n < n < n\log n < n^2 < 2^n < n!.
$$

No two functions in this list share the same `Θ` class.

### Why the hierarchy works

- Every positive power of `n` eventually dominates every logarithm.
- Multiplying `n` by `log n` makes it grow faster than linear but slower than `n²`.
- An exponential with base greater than `1` eventually dominates every fixed-degree polynomial.
- `n!` eventually dominates `2ⁿ` because its later factors are all larger than `2`.
